# CANDIDATE: RIBBON_SQUEEZE_VOLUME_BREAKOUT

**Filed:** 2026-09-06  
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)  
**Type:** new_trigger  
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

When the EMA ribbon contracts tightly (low volatility) and a volume surge occurs, the ensuing breakout tends to persist in the direction of ribbon slope. This captures short-term momentum after volatility compression, distinct from Bollinger Band squeezes by using EMA ribbon width and a volume‑surge trigger.

## Mechanism

Calculate ribbon width = EMA(8) − EMA(34) on 5‑minute bars. If ribbon width < 0.15×ATR(20) for three consecutive bars AND volume of the current bar > 2× average volume of the last 20 bars, then enter at the close of the breakout bar: long if EMA(8) > EMA(34) (upward slope), short if EMA(8) < EMA(34) (downward slope). Initial stop: opposite edge of the ribbon (longs: stop at EMA(34)−0.5×ATR; shorts: stop at EMA(8)+0.5×ATR). Target: 2×ATR profit target or chandelier exit after 1R profit. Regime filter: only trade when VIX < 15 to ensure meaningful compression.

2. **Sample bias:** Stage‑1 evaluation used the full available SPY 5‑minute history (approx. 16 months) with no walk‑forward split; parameters (ribbon width threshold, volume multiplier, ATR lookbacks) were selected heuristically, creating overfit risk to in‑sample noise.
3. **Out-of-sample:** NEEDS-OOS (no out‑of‑sample or walk‑forward test performed).
